Slide 1
Data Structures: Course Map
Chapter 1: arrays and linked lists
Chapter 2: stacks and queues
Chapter 3: choosing a structure

Slide 2
Chapter 1 — Arrays
Elements occupy contiguous storage.
Access by index: O(1).
Insertion at the front requires shifting elements: O(n).

Slide 3
Chapter 1 — Singly Linked Lists
Each node stores a value and a next pointer.
Access by position requires traversal: O(n).
Insertion after an already known node: O(1); finding that node is separate.

Slide 4
Chapter 2 — Stacks
Last in, first out (LIFO).
push adds to the top; pop removes the top.
Example: undo history.

Slide 5
Chapter 2 — Queues
First in, first out (FIFO).
enqueue adds at the back; dequeue removes from the front.
Example: tasks waiting for service.

Slide 6
Chapter 3 — Selection and Boundaries
Choose an array for frequent indexed reads.
Choose a stack when the most recent item must be processed first.
Choose a queue when arrival order must be preserved.
This course does not specify thread safety or memory-management policy.

Slide 7
Chapter 3 — Review
A linked-list O(1) insertion claim assumes the target node is already known.
State the operation and its assumptions when quoting complexity.
LIFO and FIFO describe removal order, not a particular storage layout.
